label: verify-bm-poc-designs

claims.claim: The law kappa = f(m,n) d_eps/h with f <= 3/2 (equality at m^2 n = 1) is reproduced by the project's check script re-run unchanged and by an independent layered-beam solver to 1e-9, so a bilayer's curvature is predicted with no fitted parameter once free strains and thicknesses are measured.
claims.source_says: VERDICT: the ceiling holds in every check (best of 4000 hill-climbs from random starts: f = 1.500000000000). Saved solver_vs_f: solver and f_project agree to 9 decimals at 7 points.
claims.note: The script re-run and the solver agreement reproduce, but I did not re-derive the solver; 'no fitted parameter' is a framing that also assumes perfect bond, small strain and measured free strains.

claims.claim: All predictions rest on the Flexible 80A V2 row: +8% mass/+3% volume at 1 day, +9%/+7% at 1 week in deionized water, giving 1-3% linear strain; no independent measurement of hygroscopic strain or diffusivity exists in the sources read.
claims.note: I fetched the PDF and the water row matches; 1.03^(1/3)-1=0.99% and 1.07^(1/3)-1=2.28% reproduce; the 'no other measurement' part is a negative about the agent's reading, and 'every prediction' also leans on moduli and D priors.

claims.claim: Only soft-on-soft pairs (80A V2 with Flexible 50A or Silicone 40A) reach 99% of the 3/2 ceiling at printable thickness; stiff partners lose 41% (Tough 1000) to 89% (Rigid 10K).
claims.source_says: Stress at 50% Elongation 1.5 MPa 2.9 MPa (80A V2 data sheet, ASTM D412). Data sheet gives no tensile modulus; wet 3.0 MPa and partner moduli are the agent's own estimates.
claims.note: With the agent's assumed moduli my independent beam calculation gives f = 1.495, 1.493, 0.883, 0.499, 0.162, so the arithmetic holds, but the moduli inputs are secant guesses and I did not re-read the Tough 1000, Grey V5 or Rigid 10K sheets.

claims.claim: At the optimum, curvature settles in 0.719 h_a^2/D; the Formlabs 1-day/1-week data give D between 1.4e-12 and 9.3e-12 m2/s for an assumed 2 mm slab, so a 0.4 mm layer settles in hours to about a day, the louver blade in 1-10 days, a metre-scale element in months.
claims.source_says: Rectangular slabs, used for hardness, mass, and volume change, are evaluated immediately after wiping dry without a conditioning period.
claims.note: I reproduced 0.719 (t90) and 1.652 (t99) with my own Fourier moment model, and D = 9.3e-12 (mass) and 1.4e-12 (volume) for 2 mm, but the sheet states no slab thickness, so D and every time rests on an assumed 2 mm and Fickian behaviour.

overall: All four key claims hold up arithmetically. I confirmed the water row in the Formlabs PDF and reproduced the ceiling script verdict, the partner table and the 0.719 and 1.65 settling numbers independently. The caveats are inputs, not arithmetic. The slab thickness, the wet and partner moduli, and the isotropic and Fickian assumptions are the agent's own, not the data sheet's.
